request: Fix the product data-directory lock race before another stable release; user explicitly approved SQLite-backed locking and Node.js 22.5+ compatibility change.
rootCause: The old algorithm could classify an old owner as stale, then observe/claim the replacement directory and remove its live owner. The forced-interleaving regression reports two successful holders against the unchanged base implementation.
implementation: Keep BEGIN IMMEDIATE on owner-private run/instance-lock.sqlite for the entire product lifetime, including marker inspection, creation and removal.
Never remove/replace the SQLite lock database on normal release; process exit or SIGKILL releases the OS transaction lock.
Refuse same-process ownership by canonical run-directory path before opening filesystem descriptors for lock-database initialization.
Retain the legacy owner marker, live-PID protection and unfinished-marker grace period. Recover stale legacy markers, including abandoned recovery.claim files, only under the SQLite lock.
Reject symlink, hardlink, non-file or foreign-owner lock databases; normalize permissions to 0600.
Update packaged engine metadata, doctor, install guidance and installed-package smoke coverage without a dependency or Runtime pin change.
